report.answer_text:
Tower cranes are standard engineering equipment, so I'm answering from general knowledge and didn't search.
Main structural parts
Base / Foundation
A concrete slab, often with anchor bolts or a fixing angle set into it. It carries the crane's weight and the loads it lifts, and it keeps the crane stable.
Some cranes use a travelling (rail) base instead, or are tied to the building.
Mast (tower)
A vertical lattice steel column built from bolted or pinned sections.
It gives the crane its height and carries the vertical loads down to the base.
Extra sections are added as the building rises. This is called "climbing."
Slewing unit (slewing ring and motor)
It sits at the top of the mast.
It lets the crane's upper part rotate through 360°, powered by slew motors and gearboxes.
Operator's cab
It is usually mounted next to or just below the slewing unit.
It holds the controls, a load-moment display and a view of the work area. Some cranes are run by remote control instead.
Jib (working arm)
It is the long horizontal arm that carries the trolley and extends the crane's reach.
Its length sets the crane's working radius.
Counter-jib (machinery arm)
It is the shorter arm on the opposite side of the jib.
It carries the counterweights, the hoisting winch and the motors.
Counterweights
They are concrete or steel blocks on the counter-jib.
They balance the load on the jib so the crane doesn't tip.
Tower head / Apex (cathead)
It is the peak above the slewing unit.
Tie bars or pendant lines run from it to the jib and counter-jib to support them.
Lifting and moving parts
Trolley
It runs along the underside of the jib and moves the load in and out, changing the working radius.
Hoist winch and drum
It is on the counter-jib.
It winds the hoist rope in and out to raise and lower the load.
Hoist rope (wire rope)
Steel cable that runs from the winch over the trolley to the hook block.
Hook block (hook and pulleys)
It is the assembly that hangs from the trolley.
It holds the load, and its pulleys give mechanical advantage.
Tie bars / Pendants
Rods or cables that hold the jib and counter-jib up from the apex.
Safety and control systems
Load moment limiter (LML): It stops the crane lifting loads that are too heavy for the current radius.
Limit switches: They restrict hook height, trolley travel and slewing.
Anemometer: It measures wind speed and warns the operator when it gets dangerous.
Brakes and weathervane (free-slew) mode: They hold the load in place. When the crane is out of service, the jib can turn freely so it points downwind.
Aviation lights and warning devices: They make the crane visible.
Climbing / extension parts
Climbing frame (jacking cage): It is a collar around the top of the mast.
Hydraulic jack: It lifts the crane's upper section so a new mast section can be inserted.
Tie-ins / collars: Brackets that fix the mast to the building for extra stability on very tall cranes.
I can go into more detail on any of these. I could also cover how the climbing process works or the main crane types, such as hammerhead, luffing-jib and self-erecting.
